ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Separate scales for camera and register tokens in eight-bit VGGT
PROPOSAL: We quantize the weights of VGGT to eight bits per output channel and its activations to eight bits per tensor, with the camera and register tokens receiving a scale estimated apart from the image tokens in each transformer block. Calibration draws 32 sequences of eight frames from CO3Dv2 training categories. We report camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on held-out CO3Dv2 categories and 7-Scenes, and point map accuracy and completeness on DTU, always against the full-precision model, using three independent calibration draws to show the spread between selections.
CONTROLS: Round-to-nearest with one shared scale for all tokens, SmoothQuant migration under a shared scale, and GPTQ weights with plain activation scaling. One ablation gives separate scales inside global attention blocks alone. A latency check measures forward time at batch size one with integer kernels on a single accelerator, taking the median over many forward passes.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Separate scales should keep pose AUC within one point of full precision where the shared scale loses several points. The gain may vanish if register token outliers are mild at eight bits.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bit-width and granularity study for post-training quantization of VGGT
PROPOSAL: We quantize VGGT with weights at four, six and eight bits and activations at six, eight and sixteen bits, under per-tensor, per-channel and per-group scales, and fit static ranges for each block of the aggregator and each prediction head from calibration pools of sixteen, thirty-two and sixty-four sequences from CO3Dv2. Each setting is calibrated with five independent draws. We report camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and 7-Scenes, point map accuracy and completeness on DTU, and depth error on ScanNet, against full precision. Pools are stratified by dataset and by sequence length before each draw.
CONTROLS: Round-to-nearest, SmoothQuant, GPTQ and activation-aware weight quantization run at each setting. Ablations remove the separate camera-token range, the separate register-token range and the per-head range one at a time. Latency with integer kernels is timed at three batch sizes on one accelerator.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Lower precision settings should degrade pose accuracy steadily, with per-group scales recovering most of the loss at four-bit weights. Differences between calibration pool sizes should be small.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rotation-based outlier smoothing for six-bit activations in VGGT
PROPOSAL: We insert orthogonal Hadamard rotations before the query, key and value projections and before the feed-forward input of each aggregator block, fusing the inverse into adjacent weights so that inference cost stays unchanged. Weights use per-channel six-bit scales found by GPTQ, and activations use six-bit per-token scales. Calibration uses 64 sequences from RealEstate10K. We measure pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and RealEstate10K held-out scenes, point map Chamfer distance on ETH3D, and activation kurtosis at the camera and register token positions before and after rotation.
CONTROLS: GPTQ without rotation, SmoothQuant, a rotation applied to image tokens alone, and a random orthogonal matrix in place of the Hadamard one. The full-precision model is the reference, and memory is measured with the integer weights packed.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Rotation should cut kurtosis at special token positions several-fold and hold pose AUC within two points of full precision. It may fail where outliers sit in a few fixed channels that the transform does not mix.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Smoothing and rotation recipes for low-bit activations in VGGT
PROPOSAL: We compare channel smoothing at three migration strengths with Hadamard rotations and random orthogonal rotations, applied to the aggregator blocks, the camera head and the three dense heads, with weights at four or eight bits and activations at six or eight bits. Ranges come from calibration pools drawn separately from CO3Dv2, RealEstate10K and ScanNet, and each recipe is rerun with three calibration draws. We report pose AUC at 30 degrees, point map Chamfer distance, depth error and tracking accuracy on ETH3D, 7-Scenes and Sintel, plus activation statistics at all layers.
CONTROLS: GPTQ without rotation, SmoothQuant alone, rotation of image tokens only, and rotation of special tokens only. Rotation placement is varied over the query, key, value and feed-forward positions, and the full-precision model is the reference with memory measured after packing.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Rotation recipes should beat smoothing alone at six-bit activations on most datasets. The ranking among migration strengths should be unstable between datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Farthest-point selection of calibration sequences for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We build a pool of 2000 sequences from CO3Dv2, ScanNet and RealEstate10K, embed each frame with the pretrained DINO encoder inside VGGT, and choose 64 calibration sequences by greedy farthest-point selection on pooled embeddings, after rejecting the sequences whose activation norms lie in the top two percent. We quantize with eight-bit weights and six-bit activations and report pose AUC at 30 degrees and point map accuracy on held-out scenes from each source, and the spread of both over ten independent selections.
CONTROLS: Random selection, class-balanced selection, selection by embedding clusters, and farthest-point selection without outlier rejection, each with 64 sequences. A full-precision model gives the reference, and an oracle that calibrates on the evaluation scenes bounds what selection can gain.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Farthest-point selection with rejection should cut the spread over selections roughly in half relative to random draws. The mean gain may be small if random draws already cover the pool well.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration selection strategies and pool sizes for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We form pools of 500 to 4000 sequences from CO3Dv2, ScanNet, RealEstate10K, ETH3D and Tanks and Temples, embed frames with the encoder inside VGGT, and select calibration subsets of sixteen to 128 sequences by random draw, clustering, farthest-point choice, gradient norm and activation entropy. Each combination is quantized at three weight and activation precisions and rerun with ten draws. We report pose AUC at 30 degrees and point map accuracy on held-out scenes of each source. Subset overlap between selectors is tabulated for each pool size and selector pair.
CONTROLS: Random selection, class-balanced selection, outlier rejection at thresholds of one, two and five percent, and a full-precision reference. An oracle that calibrates on the evaluation scenes bounds the gain, and agreement between selectors is read from rank correlations.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Selector rankings should stay stable across pool sizes, with diminishing returns beyond 64 sequences. Entropy-based selection may be no better than random draws.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measured speed and memory of integer VGGT inference
PROPOSAL: We export the eight-bit weight and eight-bit activation VGGT to an integer inference engine and time the forward pass on an A100 and an RTX 4090, for inputs of 2, eight and 32 frames at the native resolution. We record peak memory, latency per frame and the share of time spent in global attention, then confirm that camera pose AUC and depth error on CO3Dv2 and 7-Scenes match the simulated quantization run. Special-token scales are folded into constants so that no dynamic range step is added at inference.
CONTROLS: The half-precision model with the same engine, the full-precision model, and a simulated quantization run that gives the accuracy reference. Timing uses fixed clocks, a warm-up pass and the median of 50 runs.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Integer kernels should cut memory close to half and latency by about a third at 32 frames. Speed-ups may shrink at 2 frames where attention is cheap and launch costs dominate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latency and memory profile of integer VGGT on server and edge devices
PROPOSAL: We export VGGT at eight-bit and four-bit weights with eight-bit activations to an integer inference engine and time the forward pass on an A100, an H100, an RTX 4090 and an edge module, for inputs of 2, 4, 8, 16, thirty-two and sixty-four frames at three resolutions and batch sizes of one, two and four. We record peak memory, latency per frame, per-layer time and energy, and confirm that pose AUC and depth error on CO3Dv2, seven-Scenes and ScanNet match the simulated run for each configuration.
CONTROLS: The half-precision model, the full-precision model and two alternative engines run with the same inputs. Timing uses fixed clocks, a warm-up pass and the median of 200 runs, and each measurement is rerun on a second occasion.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Integer kernels should cut memory close to half at eight bits and latency by about a third at the longest inputs. Gains at four-bit weights may be limited by dequantization cost.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sensitivity-guided mixed precision for VGGT weights
PROPOSAL: We estimate the sensitivity of each of the 24 frame and global attention blocks and of the four prediction heads using a Hessian trace computed on 128 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet, then assign four-bit or eight-bit weights to meet a size target of 40 percent of the half-precision model. Activations stay at eight bits with separate scales for the special tokens. We report pose AUC at 30 degrees, point map accuracy, depth error and tracking accuracy on five benchmarks, with calibration repeated for five draws.
CONTROLS: Uniform four-bit and uniform eight-bit weights, a random assignment of precisions at the same size, an assignment by weight magnitude, and the full-precision model. One ablation fixes the heads at eight bits to test whether head sensitivity drives the result.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Sensitivity-guided assignment should recover most of the gap between uniform four-bit and uniform eight-bit weights at the same size. The Hessian estimate may rank blocks poorly if calibration is thin.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-wise precision search over VGGT with curvature and gradient measures
PROPOSAL: We score each attention block, feed-forward layer and prediction head of VGGT with Hessian trace, gradient norm, weight kurtosis and output perturbation, each computed on calibration sets of 32 to 256 sequences from CO3Dv2, ScanNet and RealEstate10K. For each score we search assignments of 3 to eight bits at size targets of thirty to 50 percent of the half-precision model, with activations at eight bits, and report pose AUC, point map accuracy, depth error and tracking accuracy on five benchmarks, using five draws of calibration.
CONTROLS: Uniform four-bit and uniform eight-bit weights, random assignments at the same sizes, assignments by weight magnitude, and the full-precision model. Agreement between the four measures is read from rank correlations, and head and block ablations separate their roles.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Hessian trace and output perturbation should agree closely and beat magnitude-based assignment. Kurtosis may be a poor guide inside global attention blocks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pilot transfer test of language-model quantization methods to VGGT
PROPOSAL: We apply SmoothQuant, GPTQ and activation-aware weight quantization to VGGT at eight-bit weights and eight-bit activations, calibrated on 16 sequences from CO3Dv2, and measure the loss in pose AUC at 30 degrees on held-out CO3Dv2 categories. We log per-channel activation ranges at the camera and register token positions and at image token positions in three blocks, to see whether special tokens produce the heavy tails seen in language models. The pilot fixes which methods are worth carrying into a full study.
CONTROLS: Round-to-nearest as the naive floor, the full-precision model as the ceiling, and two calibration draws to see whether a method's rank flips between draws. Differences are read per method and never pooled over methods.
COST: 12
PREDICTION: Methods designed for language models should lose a few points of pose AUC at eight bits, and special tokens should show heavier tails than image tokens. All three methods may be indistinguishable at this precision.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of language and 2D vision quantization methods to VGGT on six benchmarks
PROPOSAL: We apply SmoothQuant, GPTQ, activation-aware weight quantization, PTQ4ViT, RepQ-ViT and a rotation-based method to VGGT at eight-bit and six-bit weights with eight-bit and six-bit activations, calibrated on 16, 32 and sixty-four sequences from CO3Dv2, and measure pose AUC at 30 degrees, point map accuracy, depth error and tracking accuracy on six benchmarks. We log per-channel activation ranges at special token positions and image token positions in all blocks, and rerun each method with five calibration draws.
CONTROLS: Round-to-nearest as the floor, the full-precision model as the ceiling, and a combination of the best weight method with the best activation method. Method ranks are compared across precisions and benchmarks.
COST: 12
PREDICTION: Language-model methods should lose a few points of pose AUC at eight bits and much more at six bits. Rankings may change between benchmarks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offline ranges for the data-independent special tokens of VGGT
PROPOSAL: The camera and register tokens are pretrained constants, so their first-layer activations are known before any input arrives. We compute their ranges exactly in each block by propagating the tokens through a calibration pass on 48 sequences from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet, store them as fixed scales, and keep image tokens on ranges from the same pass. We quantize to eight-bit weights and six-bit activations and report pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and 7-Scenes, plus point map accuracy on DTU, comparing the operation count with dynamic scaling.
CONTROLS: Static scales shared by all tokens, per-token dynamic scales for all tokens, per-token dynamic scales for special tokens alone, and the full-precision model. Operation counts are taken from the exported graph, and each variant is rerun with three calibration draws.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Exact fixed ranges for special tokens should match per-token dynamic scales within one point of pose AUC at no inference cost. The ranges may drift once attention mixes image information into the special tokens in deeper blocks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Static versus dynamic ranges for each token type in VGGT
PROPOSAL: We compare per-tensor static, per-token static, per-token dynamic and per-channel static activation scales on image tokens, camera tokens, register tokens and prediction head inputs of VGGT, in each of the forty-eight aggregator blocks, at six-bit and eight-bit activations with four-bit and eight-bit weights. Calibration passes use 16, forty-eight and ninety-six sequences from CO3Dv2, ScanNet and RealEstate10K, repeated with four draws, and we report pose AUC at 30 degrees, point map accuracy and depth error on CO3Dv2, seven-Scenes, DTU and NYUv2.
CONTROLS: Static scales shared by all token types, dynamic scales for all tokens, and the full-precision model. Operation counts and memory traffic are taken from the exported graph, and the placement of dynamic scales is varied block by block.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Dynamic scales on special tokens should add little accuracy over fixed ones. Per-channel scales may help only at the lowest bit width, and static per-tensor ranges should suffice for image tokens in the early blocks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Block-wise learned rounding for four-bit weights in VGGT
PROPOSAL: We reconstruct the output of each aggregator block with learned rounding of its weights at four bits, minimizing the squared error to the full-precision block output on 128 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet, with 2000 optimization steps per block and activations held at eight bits with separate special-token scales. We report pose AUC at 30 degrees, point map accuracy and depth error on CO3Dv2, 7-Scenes, DTU and ETH3D, and measure whether reconstruction error accumulates over the 24 block pairs by comparing block-wise and end-to-end output error.
CONTROLS: Round-to-nearest and GPTQ at four bits, the same reconstruction without learned rounding, and the same reconstruction using calibration sequences from a single dataset only. The full-precision model gives the reference, and three random seeds give the spread.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Learned rounding should lift pose AUC several points over GPTQ at four-bit weights. Gains may disappear if reconstruction overfits the 128 calibration sequences.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Block-wise reconstruction variants for low-bit VGGT under different loss functions
PROPOSAL: We reconstruct the output of each aggregator block and each prediction head with learned rounding at 3 to six bits, using squared error, cosine distance, Hessian-weighted error and a task loss on pose, with 500 to 8000 optimization steps and calibration sets of thirty-two to 512 sequences from CO3Dv2, ScanNet and RealEstate10K. Activations are held at eight bits. We report pose AUC at 30 degrees, point map accuracy and depth error on CO3Dv2, seven-Scenes, DTU, ETH3D and Sintel, plus the growth of output error over the block stack and its split by prediction head.
CONTROLS: Round-to-nearest and GPTQ at each bit width, the same reconstruction without learned rounding, and a single-dataset calibration variant. The full-precision model gives the reference, and three seeds give the spread for each configuration.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Learned rounding should help most at 3 bits and add little at six bits. Longer optimization may overfit the smaller calibration sets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration on indoor scenes and testing on outdoor scenes for quantized VGGT
PROPOSAL: We calibrate eight-bit weight and six-bit activation VGGT on 32 sequences from ScanNet alone, and evaluate pose AUC at 30 degrees and point map accuracy on held-out ScanNet scenes, on the outdoor sequences of KITTI and Tanks and Temples, and on object-centred CO3Dv2 sequences. The question is whether ranges fitted on indoor data stay valid under a shift in scene type. We record the fraction of activations clipped at test time in each block, as a direct signal of range mismatch.
CONTROLS: Calibration on 32 sequences from the target domain, calibration on a mixture of ScanNet and KITTI, and the full-precision model. Three calibration draws per setting give the spread, and the draw is held fixed within a setting.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Indoor ranges should lose several points of pose AUC on outdoor scenes, with clipping rising in the deeper global attention blocks. A mixed calibration set may recover most of the loss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-domain calibration matrix for quantized VGGT
PROPOSAL: We calibrate eight-bit weight and six-bit activation VGGT on 32 sequences from each of ScanNet, CO3Dv2, RealEstate10K, KITTI, Tanks and Temples, DTU and 7-Scenes, and evaluate pose AUC at 30 degrees and point map accuracy on held-out scenes of each dataset, producing a seven by seven matrix. We record the fraction of activations clipped at test time in each block of the aggregator, and repeat the matrix at four-bit weights with five draws per cell. Clipping rates are tabulated by block depth and by dataset pair for each precision.
CONTROLS: Calibration on mixtures of two, three and all seven datasets, and the full-precision model. Matrix entries are summarized by diagonal and off-diagonal means, and clipping rates are compared between source domains.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Off-diagonal entries should lose several points of pose AUC relative to the diagonal. Mixed calibration should recover most of the loss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frame-count drift of activation ranges in quantized VGGT
PROPOSAL: We calibrate the quantized VGGT on sequences of eight frames and test on sequences of 8, 16, 32 and 64 frames from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet, since global attention statistics depend on how many frames are mixed. We record activation ranges per block as the frame count grows and fit a simple correction that rescales global attention ranges by the frame count. Weights use eight bits and activations use six bits, and we report pose AUC at 30 degrees, point map accuracy and the fraction of clipped activations for each frame count over five calibration draws.
CONTROLS: Calibration at the test frame count, calibration on a mixture of 8, 16 and 32 frame sequences, the uncorrected static ranges, and the full-precision model. An ablation applies the rescaling to the last 12 blocks alone.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Static ranges fitted at eight frames should lose accuracy as sequences grow and the rescaling should recover most of it. Drift may be small if attention statistics saturate after eight frames.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frame-count and resolution robustness of quantization ranges in VGGT
PROPOSAL: We calibrate the quantized VGGT on sequences of 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 frames at three resolutions and test on all combinations of 2 to 64 frames, using CO3Dv2, ScanNet, RealEstate10K and ETH3D. We record activation ranges per block and per token type, fit corrections of several forms that rescale global attention ranges by the frame count, with weights at four or eight bits and activations at six or eight bits, and report pose AUC at 30 degrees, point map accuracy, depth error and clipped fraction over five calibration draws.
CONTROLS: Calibration at the test setting, calibration on mixtures of frame counts, uncorrected static ranges, and the full-precision model. Corrections are ablated by block depth and by token type, with each cell rerun on a second set of scenes.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Ranges fitted at few frames should lose accuracy as sequences lengthen, and the rescaling should recover most of it. Resolution should matter less than frame count.
